question: In bimanual uterine compression for atonic PPH, one hand compresses the uterine fundus externally via the abdomen while the other hand, inserted into the vagina (not the uterus), provides counter-pressure against the anterior uterine wall.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Bimanual uterine compression involves an abdominal (external) hand on the fundus and a vaginal (internal) fist providing posterior counter-pressure — the internal hand is in the vagina, not inside the uterine cavity.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The internal hand is in the VAGINA (not intrauterine) forming a fist behind the uterus, while the external abdominal hand compresses the fundus anteriorly. This creates sustained bimanual compression to stimulate uterine contraction.
